subject: Clarify: metering cliff and tiered floor behavior for long-context streaming calls
messages:
From: Sarah Lowry <sarah.lowry@elm-therapeutics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Metering questions before PO

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Procurement asked me to get a clearer note on how Redwood will bill for two specific usage patterns we expect: (1) long-context analysis where we send a ~50k token document once and ask for a multi-pass analysis (not streaming-critical), and (2) continuous streaming agents where tokens are emitted intermittently and conversations will often be <3s bursts but many bursts per hour.

Key questions they want addressed:
- For the 50k document case, is billing purely "consumed tokens" or is there a minimum per call / per-context floor that will apply? If there is a floor, how does it interact with our expected bursty follow-up prompts on the same document (prefix reuse)?
- For streaming bursts, how do you round partial token windows and do microbursts get aggregated into the session/heartbeat logic? Is there a cliff where we jump to a higher tier/floor once we exceed X tokens per minute?

We need this detail before we submit a PO—can you send a short worked example with numbers? Procurement will use it in the SOW.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lowry
Head of ML Platform
Elm Therapeutics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lowry <sarah.lowry@elm-therapeutics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Metering questions before PO

Hi Sarah — great questions, thanks. Quick answers up front and I'll follow with a short worked example: 

- 50k document multi-pass: billing is token-consumption based; however, the platform applies our "active-context" floor per-call when a call opens a new context bucket. If you send the full 50k in one call and do multiple analysis passes in the same session that reuse the KV/prefix, subsequent passes are billed only for the additional generated tokens plus any new input tokens (so you avoid repeated full-charge for the same prefix).
- Streaming microbursts: we aggregate short bursts into a rolling 60s window for rounding purposes; partial-token windows are rounded up to the nearest billing quantum (default 10 tokens) unless you opt-in to a microburst aggregation policy. There isn't a hidden cliff that instantly bumps you to a higher floor, but we do have tiered floors (e.g., standard per-call minimum vs committed tier floors) that apply depending on contract.

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with worked numbers and a draft SOW snippet that maps billable lines to examples you can drop in procurement. If you'd like, we can convert the example to your projected monthly traffic and show incremental pricing with and without a 12-month commit.

Sending the sheet now — I'll loop Marissa and pricing to propose a concession path for the PO.

Best,
Mina

Redwood Inference

- For streaming, the aggregation to 60s is helpful. Procurement is specifically worried about rounding for many tiny bursts (e.g., 5 tokens each). Can your microburst aggregation policy be applied at the account level or only per-route? We want it globally enforced for a customer experience where we don't overpay for tiny telemetry pings.

Also, is there a practical example you can show where rounding + minimums cause a 15–25% delta vs raw consumed tokens? Procurement likes to see the gap explicitly.

Folks — forwarding Elm's questions. They're scoping two concerns: long single-document multi-pass analysis and lots of microburst streaming. Procurement is sensitive to rounding and minimums. They're asking for: 1) a worked example showing raw tokens vs billed tokens (with rounding/minimums) and 2) whether we can commit to account-level microburst aggregation in contract or as a config.

Can you draft a couple of numeric scenarios and a recommended concession (e.g., reduce per-call floor for first 3 months; or a blended token rate above a threshold)? I'd like something we can put in the SOW.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Metering questions before PO — Elm Therapeutics (need numbers + concession ideas)

Mina / Marissa — drafted numbers and options below. I'll paste the short worked examples and recommended contract language.

Scenario A — 50k doc, single upload, 2 subsequent analysis passes within same sticky session (KV reuse)
- Upload input tokens: 50,000 tokens (one-time)
- First pass generates 2,500 tokens -> billed = 50,000 (input quantum rounded) + 2,500 (output) = 52,500 tokens
- Second pass reuses KV and generates 1,200 tokens -> billed = 1,200 (since prefix KV reused)
- Total billed tokens = 52,500 + 1,200 = 53,700 tokens
- Raw consumed tokens (sum of raw) = 50,000 + 2,500 + 1,200 = 53,700 -> in this example no nonlinearity because reuse prevented double-billing of input.

Note: "same session" sticky KV = 72-hour default for hosted API; this is configurable in Private/Dedicated and negotiable in SOW for enterprise. After the sticky KV expires, subsequent requests that re-ingest the full 50k will be charged again. We can offer a 7-day sticky window for Elm under a contract term.

Scenario B — streaming microbursts: example of rounding delta
- 100 bursts in an hour, each burst = 5 tokens input + 7 tokens generated = 12 raw tokens/burst -> raw tokens = 1,200
- Billing quantum = 10 tokens (default) -> each burst billed as ceil(12/10)*10 = 20 tokens -> billed per burst = 20 -> billed total = 2,000 tokens
- Delta = (2000 - 1200) / 1200 = 66.7% higher billed vs raw

Mitigations / concessions we can propose:
1) Account-level microburst aggregation: aggregate bursts into a rolling 60-second bucket for billing; so if multiple bursts fall in a bucket, we bill the bucket total (rounded once). This reduces the example above dramatically.
2) Temporary reduced billing quantum: set quantum to 5 tokens for Elm (instead of 10) for first 6 months. This reduces rounding overhead on many tiny pings.
3) Commit-tier blended rate: above 10M billed tokens/month, apply a blended token price and waive per-call minimums for streaming routes marked as telemetry.
4) Sticky KV extension: set sticky KV to 7 days in SOW for the 50k doc workflow.

Recommended SOW language snippet (short):
- "Redwood will provide a 7-day sticky KV window for Elm Therapeutics for routes used to process long-document analysis so that repeated analysis passes within 7 days reuse cached prefix and avoid recharging input tokens."
- "Redwood will apply account-level microburst aggregation (rolling 60s) for telemetry routes defined by Elm; billing quantum for these routes will be set to 5 tokens for the initial 6-month pilot."
- "If Elm commits to a 12-month consumption commit >= 10M billed tokens/month, Redwood will apply a blended token rate of $X per 1k tokens and waive per-call minimums for telemetry routes."

I'm attaching the worked spreadsheet (sheets have the numeric breakdowns) — happy to tweak numbers to Elm's projected volumes.

-Karthik

Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — attaching the worked examples and a short SOW draft for your procurement team (attached: Pricing_WorkedExamples.xlsx, SOW-Draft.pdf). Key points: 

- For long-document multi-pass: default sticky KV is 72 hours; per your ask we can extend to 7 days for Elm in the SOW so you don't pay again for reusing the same prefix within that window.
- For streaming microbursts: the raw tokens vs billed tokens can be large for many tiny pings. See Scenario B in the spreadsheet — rounding can create a ~50–70% delta for tiny bursts with default quantum. We propose account-level microburst aggregation (rolling 60s) + temporary billing quantum = 5 tokens for the pilot.
- Concession proposal we're prepared to include in the PO: 6-month reduced quantum + 7-day sticky KV; if Elm signs a 12-month commit >= 10M billed tokens/month we'll roll in the blended token price and permanently waive telemetry per-call minimums.

Next step: if this looks acceptable, can Procurement confirm 1) the telemetry routes to be covered by the microburst rule (route names or route IDs), and 2) whether Elm wants the 7-day sticky KV limited to a set of route IDs or account-wide? Once we get that I'll produce a clean SOW + redline and route the PO path to legal.

Thanks — Mina
